headline: Highest risk is data leakage: aci can egress CRM/email data while the companion list is non-runnable and network-isolated, making direct pairwise harm limited but compliance and injection pathways still plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest content via direct function calls or MCP and touches email/CRM data, so malicious instructions in shared content could be forwarded into its tool flow. The companion agent is a non-runnable reference list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot actively inject; the pathway is one-way and requires unusual bridging.
conditions: IF aci is fed untrusted email, CRM, or Slack content as instructions
IF the operator manually copies B-derived text into aci prompts or MCP inputs
mitigations: Restrict aci to structured prompts only
Add a provenance tag to all inbound text
Disable copy-paste from untrusted sources during runs
Review MCP inputs before execution
requires-engineering: add instruction/content separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches lead generation, customer support, calendar, email, and CRM data and has broad network egress, so sensitive data can leave the workspace by default. The companion agent has no data classes touched and no network egress, so it is not a leakage source; the pair risk is dominated by aci's outbound integrations.
conditions: IF aci is connected to email, CRM, Slack, Sheets, or calendar accounts containing sensitive records
IF outbound API calls are enabled without per-destination allowlisting
mitigations: Limit aci to a test tenant
Remove unnecessary API connections
Turn on destination allowlists
Redact sensitive fields before sync
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on outbound tool calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and can write through external APIs, but the companion profile is not runnable and exposes no mutable surfaces, so there is no documented shared-write conflict. Uncertainty is low because B lacks any write or network capability that could contend with A.
conditions: IF B is replaced with a runnable agent that writes to the same CRM, email, or Sheets resources
IF multiple aci instances are pointed at the same external account without coordination
mitigations: Run only one aci instance per account
Use separate test and production credentials
Add account-level locking where available
Check for duplicate writes in logs
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate or transform CRM/email/calendar content that downstream systems may treat as authoritative, so bad outputs can cascade into operational mistakes. The companion agent is a static list and cannot act, which lowers pairwise risk, but aci's outputs still need verification before any human or system uses them.
conditions: IF aci-generated text is copied into emails, CRM updates, or calendar actions without review
IF downstream automation consumes aci output as final truth
mitigations: Require human review before sending
Compare outputs against source records
Use draft-only modes for email and CRM
Log provenance for generated fields
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action APIs

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles email, CRM, customer support, and calendar data, which can include regulated personal data, while the companion profile is a non-runnable public list with no data classes. The main compliance issue is aci's cross-system handling and broad egress; B is not a direct compliance sink, but the pair still inherits aci's residency and retention exposure.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is placed into aci-connected systems
IF retention or residency requirements differ across the connected SaaS tools
mitigations: Classify data before syncing
Exclude regulated fields from aci workflows
Verify vendor DPAs and residency settings
Shorten retention in connected tools
requires-engineering: centralize compliance policy enforcement
